qualification_scope: Current saved mesh and fixed-world-frame, predominantly tensile diagnostic setup. Explicit displacement controls in the material-loading test; frozen damage during actual blade exchanges.

topology.frame: fixed world X normal; no general rotating material frame

material_loading.scope: Actual full mesh in a disclosed displacement-controlled tensile fixture: paired interface nodes prescribed, other bulk nodes retain actual masses and evolve natively. Explicit all-patch eligibility. No knife eligibility detector, free-fragment reclosure, rotating-frame or experimental material qualification.

probe_coupling.scope: Actual full tomato assembly plus synthetic dynamic probe. Real blade and robot are separate qualification.

blade.material_frame: fixed world X; no damage eligibility in this contact qualification
blade.quadrature_measure: reference material area, three-point degree-2 Gaussian rule with bounded refinement
blade.scope: Actual authored blade and complete saved tomato geometry in free dynamics. Synthetic contact/material/mass/inertia. Short contact exchange; not a full cut, robot or independent experiment.

geometry.scope: Six generated soft-triangle/blade intersection cases, 128 native field queries; no solver steps or force qualification.

supervisor.scope: Isolated diagnostic only; no robot/cutting/training validation

known_limits: Coefficients, blade mass/inertia and pressure stiffness remain synthetic.
Arbitrary material rotation and compression-plus-shear fracture remain unsupported.
Free preloaded opening/reclosure stress attempts are preserved as failures; full free-fragment self-contact and full cuts remain unqualified.
The artificial 0.7-metre soft-facet integration case retains its precision failure. Qualification uses the actual mesh, whose largest tested boundary edge is about 6.19 mm.
Swept/fast contact, long-run behavior, robot drives and interactive performance are later checks.
